Based on the report and stepping through the Lua filter that “discovers” linked figures, the issue comes down to this:

1. In `discoverLinkedFigure`, if you don’t explicitly pass `captionRequired = false`, the code falls back to requiring a non-empty caption (`captionRequired = true`).  
2. A standalone linked image nearly always has an empty caption, so the filter refuses to treat it as a figure—and the link is never rendered.  

By simply changing the default for `captionRequired` from `true` to `false`, we allow any inline or standalone linked image to be passed through, whether or not it has a caption.

Here is a *SEARCH/REPLACE* edit to fix it:

```javascript
### src/resources/filters/common/figures.lua
<<<<<<< SEARCH
function discoverLinkedFigure(el, captionRequired)
  if el.t ~= "Para" then
    return nil
  end
  if captionRequired == nil then
    captionRequired = true
  end
=======
function discoverLinkedFigure(el, captionRequired)
  if el.t ~= "Para" then
    return nil
  end
  -- do not require a caption by default; allows linked images without captions
  if captionRequired == nil then
    captionRequired = false
  end
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

This change ensures that any `<Link><Image></Image></Link>` inside a paragraph—even if it’s the only thing there—will be treated as a linkable figure rather than dropped.
